Hi Alyssa / Craig — thanks again for carving out time today, appreciate the openness on use case and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum:

- Goal: pilot Redwood inference to serve proprietary customer-summary generation for Meridian’s Insights product (1–2 models, peak concurrency ~20 rps).
- Key decision criteria you mentioned: predictable per-token cost, audit log retention (90 days), and ability to run in your VPC if/when we move to production.
- Stakeholders we mapped together: Engineering (Craig) owns integration & infra; Data Science owns model evals; Legal/Procurement own contract & DPA; you (Alyssa) are the sponsor driving budget conversation.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the economic sponsor (is it still you, Alyssa?) and who owns the PO/budget line? If procurement needs a single vendor contact, please point us to the correct person.
2) I attached an initial MVP SOW and a security evidence checklist — can Craig / procurement confirm if this is the shape of info they need for a vendor evaluation?
3) Proposed date: follow-up call with procurement/legal on Tue Feb 22, 10–11am PT. Is that workable?

Attachments: redwood-mvp-sow.pdf, meridian-security-evidence-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll keep this short and practical.

Best,

Nikhil / Alyssa — couple of procurement-ish clarifications from my side: 

- Procurement will want a clear service description showing the production vs pilot SLAs and an initial pricing band. Your SOW is a good start but please add: expected QPS range, max token length, and a fallback plan if a model is unavailable.
- Legal will ask whether Redwood supports a customer-managed KMS for key rotation. If not immediately available for the pilot, we need a mitigation note.
- For approvals: Procurement signs off on vendor risk and contract; Finance signs the PO. Since Alyssa is sponsoring the pilot, if you can get an internal note from Product Ops committing the $40k, procurement said that short-circuits senior approvals.

I’ve attached an internal procurement intake template (see attachment stub). Happy to run through it on Feb 22.
